summary.text: Thomas J. Smith, a Republican retired General Motors engineer who co-owns a salsa company, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in Michigan's 8th District to Kristen McDonald Rivet.
He won the August 2026 Republican primary with about half the vote even though he had suspended his campaign in mid-July, and his name remained on the ballot because ballots had already been printed.

paragraphs.text: Thomas J. Smith earned a bachelor's degree from Kettering University and a graduate degree from Michigan State University.
He worked as an engineer at General Motors before retiring and is a small business owner who co-owns a salsa company, according to news reports.

Smith entered the 2026 Republican primary for Michigan's 8th District against Trump-endorsed Amir Hassan and Al Lemmo. He suspended his campaign in mid-July and endorsed Lemmo, but his name remained on the ballot.

On August 4, 2026, he won the primary with 50.4% of the vote, ahead of Hassan (about 33%) and Lemmo, and became the party's nominee against Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet. In a statement he said he was "humbled and honored that Republicans have chosen me to take the fight to Kristen McDonald Rivet."
His campaign website described his approach as conservative leadership guided by the Constitution, faith and freedom.
He received 41.9% of the vote to Kristen McDonald Rivet's 55.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Republican Congressional candidate wins 8th district primary even though he dropped out
